judgements.justification: No praise rests on a wrong factual claim; XqTW's misread (AURC mismatch) was a criticism, and bohc's 7 is generic, not factually wrong.
omcp never acknowledged that the rebuttal answered its cons; it kept the 5 with no reason, not on new grounds.
Both committees saw the same rebuttal results (lending scenario, AdvProp); A's AC did not refuse promised fixes as the basis of reject.
No reviewer stated a position different from their rating.
Neither AC called in an extra reviewer.
All reviewers had confidence 4 and clarity was not a deciding issue in either committee.
XqTW and qDh3 both stated why they raised; no rating rose silently against its text.
A's AC counted omcp's unengaged 5 as support, and B had no silent detractor to set aside.
No reviewer in either committee rated above 7; PoYC's 7 in A matches B's 7s.
No reviewer admitted reading only part of the paper.
The split is technical depth versus problem framing within one field, not a different theoretical school.
B's meta-review stated a case for the tier, the AC's own view that the method is 'elegant' and 'very well received' (R02), not a doubt or bare acceptance.
Both committees knew the attack literature: UycQ named FGSM, PGD and Ovadia; qDh3 named FGSM, CW and MMA.
A's AC wrote that omcp 'supported the concern' and that all reviewers want more evaluations, though PoYC raised to 7 and omcp gave no reason, toward the reject.
No reviewer or AC in either committee called the paper narrow or suited to another venue.
B's chair recommended a spotlight with no detractor to answer; A's misreading omcp led to reject, not an acceptance-only argument.
The lending scenario and AdvProp results that moved scores reached both committees; no one-forum result changed one committee's ratings against the other.
Every reviewer had confidence 4; no single expert review was outweighed.
No reviewer added an objection or cut a score after the response period.
A's reviewers were more critical in text (UycQ's missing baselines), so the rating gap reflects a different judgement, not scoring leniency.
Neither committee judged the headline claim overstated; omcp's regression point is a side claim and A rejected on missing baselines.
No committee had flat marginal scores from reviewers unable to check the core; all were confidence 4 and engaged the method.
